review_notes: Reviewed the whole file. I focused on the simp lemmas mabs_mem_iff (and its additive version), isCoatom_comap and isCoatom_map. I grepped Mathlib for uses of isCoatom_map and isCoatom_comap. Only the lemma's own definition mentions isCoatom_map, so no downstream use depends on its current form. I did not run Lean. The claim that the codomain is the coerced subgroup `↥H` comes from reading the `variable (H : Subgroup G)` declaration and from the absence of any local binder named H in isCoatom_map. isCoatom_comap, by contrast, rebinds H as `{H : Type*} [Group H]`.

findings.excerpt:
theorem isCoatom_map (f : G ≃* H) {K : Subgroup G} :
    IsCoatom (Subgroup.map (f : G →* H) K) ↔ IsCoatom K :=
findings.problem: The simp lemma is accidentally specialised. Unlike isCoatom_comap, it does not bind a fresh `{H : Type*} [Group H]`. So `H` is the section variable `(H : Subgroup G)`, and `G ≃* H` means `G ≃* ↥H`. The lemma has an extra explicit argument `H` and only matches maps into a subgroup subtype of G. It does not match a general `f : G ≃* H'` between groups. A @[simp] lemma with this restricted left-hand side will almost never fire. It is also not the mirror of isCoatom_comap, which is stated for arbitrary codomains.
findings.proposed_change: Bind the codomain locally, as isCoatom_comap does: `theorem isCoatom_map {H : Type*} [Group H] (f : G ≃* H) {K : Subgroup G} : IsCoatom (Subgroup.map (f : G →* H) K) ↔ IsCoatom K`. The proof `OrderIso.isCoatom_iff (f.mapSubgroup) K` should be unchanged. This also removes the spurious explicit subgroup argument.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then rewrite `IsCoatom (K.map ↑f)` to `IsCoatom K` for any group isomorphism. This matches the intent of the @[simp] attribute and gives a symmetric map/comap interface. Callers no longer have to supply an irrelevant `H : Subgroup G`.
